headings.homecare_unnamed: Caring for your pet’s teeth at home
headings.teamNote: A note from your veterinary team

homecareTips.brushing: Daily tooth brushing with a pet-safe toothpaste is the single most effective thing you can do.
homecareTips.products: Dental diets, chews, and water additives with the VOHC seal help between brushings.
homecareTips.warningSigns: Watch for bad breath, drooling, dropping food, or pawing at the mouth — call us if you notice any.

homecareTipsEquine.checkups: Most horses need a dental check every 6 to 12 months; young and older horses may need more frequent care.
homecareTipsEquine.forage: Allow plenty of forage — long-stem hay and grazing keep the teeth wearing evenly.
homecareTipsEquine.warningSigns: Watch for dropping feed, weight loss, slow eating, head tossing or resistance to the bit, bad breath or nasal discharge — call us if you notice any.
